description: Two-panel composite of bright-field TEM micrographs showing deformation microstructures near grain boundaries in Fe-30.5Mn-8Al-1C (wt%) austenitic low-density steel after tension-tension fatigue at Δσ/2 = 315 MPa; each panel carries a 1 µm scale bar at bottom right and a letter label (a)/(b) in the top-left corner. (a) is the 550-6 sample: the grain interior contains fine parallel dark striations labelled "Planar slip bands" in blue lettering, and blue dashed lines trace slip-band traces meeting a grain boundary and continuing into the neighbouring grain, i.e. slip transfer across the boundary; the two adjoining grains are the soft-oriented and hard-oriented grains named in the caption. (b) is the 650-6 sample: a continuous bright coarse precipitate layer decorating the boundary is marked "Intergranular κ" with three orange arrows, while dark, heavily strained zones in the grain interior are marked "Dislocation pile-ups" with two magenta arrows. The figure's argument: uniform intragranular κ-carbides in 550-6 permit organized planar slip and relatively easy slip transfer, whereas coarse intergranular κ in 650-6 blocks slip and produces pile-ups. No numeric values are printed on either panel.

subfigures.description: Bright-field TEM micrograph of the 550-6 sample with a 1 µm scale bar; fine parallel dark striations in the grain interior are labelled "Planar slip bands" in blue, and blue dashed lines trace band traces across a grain boundary into the adjacent grain, indicating slip transfer between a soft-oriented and a hard-oriented grain.

Bright-field TEM micrograph of the 650-6 sample with a 1 µm scale bar; a bright, continuous coarse precipitate film along the grain boundary is labelled "Intergranular κ" with three orange arrows, and dark strained regions in the grain interior are labelled "Dislocation pile-ups" with two magenta arrows.

observations.observation: The figure consists of two bright-field TEM micrographs of grain-boundary regions in fatigued Fe-30.5Mn-8Al-1C steel, each with a 1 µm scale bar.
Panel (a) is annotated "Planar slip bands" in blue lettering over a set of fine, closely spaced parallel striations within the grain interior.
Panel (a) contains blue dashed lines that trace slip-band traces across a boundary region and into the adjacent grain, marking the geometry of slip transfer across a grain boundary.
Panel (b) is annotated "Dislocation pile-ups" in magenta/pink lettering with two magenta arrows pointing at dark, heavily strained zones adjacent to the boundary.
Panel (b) is annotated "Intergranular κ" in orange lettering with three orange arrows pointing at a bright, coarse, semi-continuous precipitate layer decorating the grain boundary.
No numeric values, axis scales, diffraction patterns or inset patterns are printed on either micrograph; the only quantitative markers are the two 1 µm scale bars.
The caption states that (a) is the 550-6 sample and (b) is the 650-6 sample, both fatigued at Δσ/2 = 315 MPa.
The caption labels the grains adjacent to the boundary as "Soft-oriented grain" and "Hard-oriented grain"; these two labels are not legible in the supplied crops of the panels.

The citing text states that in the 550-6 sample κ-carbides are uniformly distributed within the grains with no coarse precipitation at the grain boundaries, allowing organized planar slip bands and relatively uniform slip transfer across grain boundaries.

The citing text states that the 650-6 sample exhibits coarse intergranular κ-carbide precipitation that disrupts grain-boundary continuity and acts as a strong slip barrier, intensifying dislocation pile-ups and tangled wavy-slip structures.

Taken together, the two panels contrast the same boundary condition in two samples: fine intragranular precipitation accompanied by planar slip bands (a) versus coarse intergranular κ accompanied by dislocation pile-ups (b), which the citing text links to earlier crack nucleation and shortened fatigue life in 650-6.
